rem:q-metric-contact-deformation:
Remark q-deformation as a contact metric change (Miranda picture). The Cardona–Miranda–Peralta-Salas–Presas [cardona2021] procedure bridges steady Euler flow and contact-Reeb flow through a conformal change of metric. Given a divergence-free, non-vanishing Euler field X on (M^3, g), rescaling X \mapsto X / |X|_g^2 and factoring the metric maps X to the Reeb vector field of a contact form on (M^3, \tilde g). The dynamical universality derives from the contact structure, not the initial metric.

The QOU executes exactly this operation via the aether parameter q. The q-Navier–Stokes equation replaces the classical Riemannian inner product with the q-deformed Frobenius pairing (Frobenius–Hopf aether). This constitutes a one-parameter family of metric adjustments, smoothly modulating between:

  • the full Levi-Civita connection (the "Euler-side" geometry representing Riemannian fluid flow), and
  • its Reeb projection along \xi_q (the "contact-side" geometry isolating pure Reeb flow).

The parameter q acts as the dial. Three regimes govern the behaviour:

Parameter limit Geometric picture Dynamical content
q \to 1^+ Full Riemannian metric; \varTheta_q degenerates Inviscid Euler limit (\nu_q \to 0, or fixed-viscosity Navier--Stokes after c_q-rescaling); Reeb projection vanishes
q > 1 generic Strict contact metric on \mathcal{S} q-NS conditionally regular (global regularity); Reeb flow Turing-complete (Reeb universal computer)
q \to \infty Pure Reeb (horizontal components vanish) Hamiltonian first-return; bare tape-reading dynamics

A geometric reading of the q-NS obstruction. The NS obstruction class gauges how the classical q = 1 contact form collapses at a vortex-collision locus. Through Miranda's framework, increasing q past 1 rescales the Riemannian metric to buoy the contact form against degeneracy. Because the plane field \ker\varTheta = \xi^\perp on the three-dimensional flow domain has Levi datum given by the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi rather than an eigenvalue pair or condition number (core Levi form), this rescaling cannot be read as quantum pressure bounding a Levi condition number away from zero; how the q-deformation acts on \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi is not established here.

Location in the proof strategy. The q-NS research programme incorporates two implications:

  1. Global well-posedness for q > 1 (thm:q-ns-wellposedness) versus breakdown at q = 1 is a feature of the smooth-vs-degenerate contact dichotomy, not an independent quantum effect.
  2. The Levi degeneracy conjecture asks whether vanishing of \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi on the high-vorticity set prevents blow-up; that question is open, whereas the converse claim that preserving contact non-degeneracy forces blow-up is refuted by steady Beltrami flows. The Biot–Savart and hyperbolic overlap remarks give the core aspect ratio as the solution of ODEs; that ratio carries no Levi information.

In the Cardona–Miranda grammar: the parameter q selects the contact metric, and that choice determines whether the Reeb dynamics persists.
prose:outro-fluid-dynamics:
Chapter close — Fluid Dynamics of the Brane.

This chapter has developed the q-deformed Navier--Stokes model on the brane, separating its proved algebraic structure and conditional q > 1 regularity framework from the open analytical questions surrounding its q \to 1^+ degeneration.

The next chapter (Stochastic Mechanics) develops the Markov-trace transition dynamics on the same categorical state space, connecting the q-shell hierarchy and classical-limit degeneration to Nelson-type stochastic processes and adelic q \to 1 limits.
sec:stochastic-mechanics-prose-intro:
This chapter develops the stochastic-mechanics interpretation of the QOU framework. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M packages braid-word combinatorics into a class function and produces the Jones polynomial in the Hecke quotient. It admits an interpretation as a transition kernel of a stochastic dynamics on the categorical state space.

In the classical limit q \to 1, this dynamics recovers Brownian motion on the brane. At q = q_0, it produces the Nelson-style stochastic mechanics underlying the wave-particle duality and the Madelung representation of the brane fluid.
prose:intro-markov-axioms-braid-link:
Markov's theorem states that two braid words have isotopic closures iff they differ by a finite sequence of conjugation and stabilisation moves. This section promotes Markov's theorem to a categorical setting. This section fixes the bar involution that acts on the aether-level Markov trace and enumerates the braid-link bijection that drives the counting arguments.

The first blocks establish the polynomial bar involution and its Leibniz decomposition. The middle blocks enumerate the closure types (knot, link, mutually disjoint) and record the aether-level character of each. The closing blocks specialise to the small-n cases that drive the explicit binding-energy formulas, including cases where the Markov-trace ambiguity propagates and must be resolved by parity classification downstream.

The output is the categorical braid-link enumeration with explicit aether-trace evaluations. This is the combinatorial engine. Every closed-form prediction below relies on knowing both the count and the trace value for each braid-link equivalence class.

prop:polynomial-bar-involution:
Proposition Polynomial bar-involution on R[X] via X \mapsto -X with bar-symmetric subring R[X^2]. Let R be a commutative ring and R[X] its polynomial ring in one indeterminate. The map

\overline{(\cdot)} \colon R[X] \to R[X], \qquad p(X) \mapsto p(-X)

is a ring involution. Under this bar:

  • the indeterminate X is bar-anti-symmetric (\overline X = -X);
  • every constant c \in R \hookrightarrow R[X] is bar-symmetric;
  • every even-degree monomial X^{2n} is bar-symmetric;
  • every odd-degree monomial X^{2n+1} is bar-anti-symmetric;
  • the bar-symmetric subring contains R[X^2], and equals it when 2 is not a zero divisor in R. Over \mathbb{F}_2 the inclusion is strict, since X = -X there.

Categorical role

This is the canonical non-trivial bar-involution in QOU. It provides a concrete categorical setting where the polynomial indeterminate X plays the role of the bar-anti-symmetric Hecke skein

h \;=\; q - q^{-1},

with the correct bar-action h \mapsto -h matching the general definition (Bar-involution and its P_{\mathrm{avg}} / P_{\mathrm{skew}} projections).

The work is in R[X] rather than directly with the Hecke skein for three reasons. First, algebraic decidability: the substitution identities for polynomial composition give the four ring-involution axioms directly. Second, no analysis is needed: unlike \mathbb{C} with conjugation, the bar map is defined by formal substitution. Third, concrete bar-symmetric subring identification: when 2 is not a zero divisor in R, the bar-symmetric subring is exactly R[X^2], providing a concrete model of "P_{\mathrm{avg}} kills odd powers".

Proved identities

The identities established for the polynomial bar are collected in Table. All proofs use only the substitution identities for polynomial composition.

Connection to the three-layer synthesis

In the bar-symmetric three-layer synthesis, the universal kernel is bar-anti-symmetric. The polynomial indeterminate X is the canonical such kernel. The series, phase, and gain layers are all even-power polynomials in X, hence in R[X^2]. Each layer functor is concretely realised as a bar-Hecke functor on R[X] sending bar-anti-symmetric inputs to bar-symmetric outputs. The data of the synthesis become explicit elements of R[X^2].

Proofs

The core bar-involution proofs use only the four ring-involution axioms plus the substitution identities for polynomial composition.

Core bar-involution axioms

\overline X = -X.
prf:polynomial-bar-involution:
Proof Proof of polynomial bar involution. By definition \overline p := p.\mathrm{comp}(-X); applying to p = X gives X.\mathrm{comp}(-X) = -X. \square

Proposition. \overline{-X} = X. Proof. (-X).\mathrm{comp}(-X) = -(X.\mathrm{comp}(-X)) = -(-X) = X, since composition commutes with negation and -(-X) = X. \square

Proposition. \overline{C c} = C c. Proof. Constants are bar-fixed: (C c).\mathrm{comp}(-X) = C c, since substitution does not affect constants. \square

Proposition. \overline{p+q} = \overline p + \overline q. Proof. Composition distributes over addition: (p+q).\mathrm{comp}(r) = p.\mathrm{comp}(r) + q.\mathrm{comp}(r). \square

Proposition. \overline{p \cdot q} = \overline p \cdot \overline q. Proof. Composition distributes over multiplication: (p q).\mathrm{comp}(r) = p.\mathrm{comp}(r) \cdot q.\mathrm{comp}(r). \square

Proposition. \overline 1 = 1 and \overline 0 = 0. Proof. The constants 1 and 0 are unchanged by substitution. \square

Proposition. \overline{\overline p} = p. Proof. (p.\mathrm{comp}(-X)).\mathrm{comp}(-X) = p.\mathrm{comp}((-X).\mathrm{comp}(-X)) = p.\mathrm{comp}(X) = p, by associativity of composition, \overline{-X} = X, and p.\mathrm{comp}(X) = p. \square

Power identities

Proposition. \overline{X^2} = X^2. Proof. X^2 = X \cdot X, so \overline{X^2} = \overline X \cdot \overline X = (-X)(-X) = X^2. \square

Proposition. \overline{X^n} = (-1)^n \cdot X^n. Proof. Induction on n. Base (n=0): \overline 1 = 1. Step: \overline{X^{k+1}} = \overline{X \cdot X^k} = (-X) \cdot (-1)^k X^k = (-1)^{k+1} X^{k+1}. \square

Proposition. \overline{X^{2n}} = X^{2n}. Proof. From the power identity \overline{X^n} = (-1)^n X^n: coefficient is (-1)^{2n} = ((-1)^2)^n = 1. \square

Proposition. \overline{X^{2n+1}} = -X^{2n+1}. Proof. From the power identity \overline{X^n} = (-1)^n X^n: coefficient is (-1)^{2n+1} = -1. \square

Scalar identities

Proposition. Every natural-number scalar is bar-fixed in R[X]. Proof. Induction on n. Base: \overline 0 = 0. Step: \overline{k+1} = \overline k + \overline 1 = k + 1. \square

Proposition. \overline{p - q} = \overline p - \overline q. Proof. p - q = p + (-1) \cdot q; bar commutes with + and \cdot, and \overline{-1} = -1 (composition commutes with negation and fixes 1). \square

Proposition. \overline{-p} = -\overline p. Proof. Take p = 0 in the subtraction identity: \overline{-q} = \overline{0 - q} = 0 - \overline q = -\overline q. \square

Concrete bar-symmetric polynomials

Proposition. \overline{4 + X^2} = 4 + X^2. Proof. \overline 4 = 4 since natural-number scalars are bar-fixed (with 4 = (4:\mathbb{N})); \overline{X^2} = X^2; combine by additivity. \square

Proposition. The polynomial c_5^{[6]}(X) := -\tfrac{5}{4} - \tfrac{X^2}{16} + \tfrac{X^4}{64} - \tfrac{X^6}{256} is bar-symmetric. Proof. Every term has the form C(c) \cdot X^{2k} with c \in \mathbb{R} and k \in \{0,1,2,3\}. Constants are bar-fixed; even powers are bar-fixed. Sum and difference of bar-symmetric is bar-symmetric. \square

Proposition. \cos^{[6]}(X) := 1 - X^2/2 + X^4/24 - X^6/720 and \cosh^{[6]}(X) := 1 + X^2/2 + X^4/24 + X^6/720 are bar-symmetric. Proof. Same structure as the previous proposition for c_5^{[6]}: each term C(c) \cdot X^{2k} with bar-fixed coefficient and bar-fixed even power. \square

Theorem. All three layer truncations — series c_5^{[6]}, phase \cos^{[6]}, gain \cosh^{[6]} — are bar-symmetric in the same polynomial ring \mathbb{R}[X] under the same bar-involution X \mapsto -X. Proof. Conjunction of the three propositions above. The three layer avatars live in the same ambient ring with the same bar — this is the categorical-derivation unification at the truncated-polynomial level. \square

Pre-archimedean generic versions

Proposition. Over any commutative ring R (no field needed), the polynomial c_0 + c_1 X^2 + c_2 X^4 + c_3 X^6 is bar-symmetric for arbitrary c_0, c_1, c_2, c_3 \in R. Proof. Per-term: C(c_i) is bar-fixed as a constant; X^{2k} is bar-fixed as an even power. The sum is bar-symmetric by additivity. No archimedean structure invoked. \square

Theorem. For any n \in \mathbb{N} and any c : \mathbb{N} \to R, the polynomial P_n(X) := \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} c_k X^{2k} is bar-symmetric. Proof. Induction on n. Base: empty sum = 0 bar-symmetric. Step: P_{k+1} = P_k + C(c_k) X^{2k}; IH gives P_k bar-symmetric, per-term argument gives C(c_k) X^{2k} bar-symmetric; sum bar-symmetric. Holds for arbitrary truncation degree over any CommRing. \square

Theorem. Sums of odd-power monomials with arbitrary R-coefficients are bar-anti-symmetric. Proof. Induction analogous to even case, using \overline{X^{2n+1}} = -X^{2n+1} to flip sign on each term. \square

Evaluations

Proposition. c_5^{[6]}(0) = -5/4. Proof. All positive-degree terms vanish at X = 0; constant term is -5/4. \square

Proposition. c_5^{[6]}(1) = -333/256. Proof. -5/4 - 1/16 + 1/64 - 1/256 = -320/256 - 16/256 + 4/256 - 1/256 = -333/256. Approximates exact c_5(1) = -13/10 = -332.8/256 with relative error \approx 0.06\% (consistent with O(X^8 / 4^4) Taylor truncation at X = 1). \square

Future extensions: the rational-function field \mathrm{Frac}(R[X]), for rational-function functors realising the proved closed form c_5 = -3/2 + 1/(X^2 + 4), and the formal power-series ring R[[X]], for the formal power-series limit of the truncated avatars.

prf:c5-involution-leibniz-decomposition:
Proof Proof of c5 involution leibniz decomposition. Sketch.

Step 1: bar involution and the averaged crossing

The Hecke algebra H_n(q) carries the bar involution \overline{\,\,}, a \mathbb{Z}-linear anti-ring-automorphism defined by:

\overline{q} = q^{-1}, \quad \overline{\sigma_i} = \sigma_i^{-1}.

Using the Hecke quadratic \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 (where h = q - q^{-1}), \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h.

The bar-invariant projector is P_{\text{avg}} = (1 + \overline{\,\,})/2. Its action on \sigma_i gives:

P_{\text{avg}}(\sigma_i) \;=\; \frac{\sigma_i + \overline{\sigma_i}}{2}
\;=\; \frac{\sigma_i + \sigma_i^{-1}}{2}
\;=\; \frac{\sigma_i + \sigma_i - h}{2}
\;=\; \sigma_i - \frac{h}{2}.

This is the averaged crossing operator \sigma_{\text{avg}} used in the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 braid recipe.

Step 2: averaged crossings in the typed braid

From Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay, the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 proton braid uses ONE averaged \sigma_1:

\mathcal{B}_p \;=\; \sigma_0 \cdot (\sigma_1 - \tfrac{h}{2}\mathbf{1})
\;=\; \sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_{1,\text{avg}}.

The typed neutron braid uses TWO averaged crossings (one at \sigma_0, one at \sigma_1):

\mathcal{B}_n \;=\; (\sigma_0 - \tfrac{h}{2}\mathbf{1}) \cdot (\sigma_1 - h\mathbf{1})
\;=\; \sigma_{0,\text{avg}} \cdot \sigma_1^{-1}.

Each averaged crossing contributes a factor of h/2 = 1/2 at the specific position where it appears.

Step 3: Leibniz propagation to higher rungs

The categorical Markov-trace expansion of the typed braid in powers of h generates the single-wrap baseline (Form A) plus the precision-ladder corrections. The h/2 contributions from averaged positions propagate via the Leibniz product expansion:

\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_n - \mathcal{B}_p) \;=\; \mathrm{net}(n) - \mathrm{net}(p)
\;=\; \frac{h^2}{2} - h
\;=\; \frac{h(h-2)}{2}.

The h^2/2 term is the product of TWO averaged-crossing h/2 contributions (the neutron has two such positions). The h/2 generates the 1/2 in \Delta(\mathrm{net}).

For higher rungs N = k \geq 4 of the precision ladder, the expansion of \mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta) in b \cdot \hbar_q^2 produces coefficients with two distinct categorical origins:

  • Pure-\sigma contributions: from non-averaged positions in the braid. These factor through \sigma^p \cdot b^{2m} combinatorics. At the silver ratio (\sigma-eigenvalues = 1 \pm \sqrt{2} via the Hecke quadratic Silver-ratio trace degeneracy), these reduce to Pell-Lucas-clean rationals.

  • Averaged-crossing contributions: from positions where \sigma_{\text{avg}} acts. These pick up the 1/2 fingerprint of P_{\text{avg}}. At the silver ratio they give rationals with a 1/2 component that is Pell-Lucas-incompatible.

Step 4: rung-by-rung classification

Sequential extraction of c_k via R(q_0) = \prod_k (1 + c_k b^k \hbar_q^{2k}) gives:

c_k Closed form Origin At silver ratio
c_3 -2 J_{\text{Hopf}}(q=1), pure inter-block -2 (clean)
c_4 c_3 \cdot b^4 \sigma^p \cdot b^{2m} pure -49/32 = -a_3^2/2^5 (clean)
c_5 \boxed{-b^2 - 1/2} \sigma + averaging -11/8 (1/2 OUTLIER)
c_6 c_3^2 \cdot b^2 \sigma^p \cdot b^{2m} pure 7/2 = a_3/2 (clean)

The c_5 outlier is structurally distinct because \sigma_{\text{avg}} contributions at rung 5 are dominant — at all other rungs in [3, 7], the pure-\sigma contributions dominate and the averaging contributions are subdominant. □

Proofs

Hoefsmit–Quantum-2 identity

Theorem. For all q \neq 0 in \mathbb{R},

b^2(q) \;=\; \frac{q^4 + q^2 + 1}{(q^2 + 1)^2} \;=\; 1 - \frac{1}{[2]_q^2}.

Proof. Multiply both sides by [2]_q^2 = (q + q^{-1})^2: (q^2 + 1)^2 = q^2 \cdot (q + q^{-1})^2 since (q+q^{-1})^2 = (q^2+1)^2/q^2. So b^2 = (q^4+q^2+1)/(q^2[2]_q^2). Multiply numerator and denominator of b^2 by 1/q^2: b^2 = (q^2 + 1 + q^{-2})/[2]_q^2 = ([2]_q^2 - 1)/[2]_q^2 = 1 - 1/[2]_q^2 since q^2 + 1 + q^{-2} = (q+q^{-1})^2 - 1 = [2]_q^2 - 1. \square

Corollary. c_5(q) = -3/2 + 1/[2]_q^2. Proof. Substitute b^2 = 1 - 1/[2]_q^2 into c_5 = -b^2 - 1/2: c_5 = -(1 - 1/[2]_q^2) - 1/2 = -3/2 + 1/[2]_q^2. \square

Classical-QOU limit + Wedderburn identification

Theorem. c_5(q = 1) = -5/4. Proof. At q = 1: [2]_q = 2, so [2]_q^2 = 4, 1/[2]_q^2 = 1/4, c_5(1) = -3/2 + 1/4 = -5/4. \square

Theorem. c_5(1) = -(\dim V_{(3)} + \dim V_{(2,1)})/2 + 1/4 = -5/4. Proof. The Wedderburn decomposition of \mathbb{C}[S_3] has three irreps with dimensions 1 (V_{(3)}), 2 (V_{(2,1)}), 1 (V_{(1,1,1)}). The non-sign sum is 1 + 2 = 3; half is 3/2. So -3/2 = -(\dim V_{(3)} + \dim V_{(2,1)})/2. Combine with 1/4 = 1/[2]_q^2 at q=1 to get -5/4. \square

Silver-ratio identity

Lemma. [2]_q^2 = 8 at q = 1 + \sqrt 2. Proof. [2]_{1+\sqrt 2} = (1+\sqrt 2) + 1/(1+\sqrt 2) = (1+\sqrt 2) + (\sqrt 2 - 1) = 2\sqrt 2. So [2]_q^2 = 8. \square

Theorem. b^2(1 + \sqrt 2) = 7/8. Proof. From Hoefsmit–Quantum-2 + the lemma above: b^2 = 1 - 1/[2]_q^2 = 1 - 1/8 = 7/8. \square

Corollary. c_5(\mathrm{silver}) = -11/8. Proof. From the c_5 closed form + the silver-ratio identity: c_5 = -3/2 + 1/8 = -12/8 + 1/8 = -11/8. Numerator 11 is inert in \mathbb{Z}[1+\sqrt 2] (not in Pell-Lucas closure) — the c_5 outlier fingerprint. \square

c_5 in terms of Hecke skein h

Lemma. For all q \neq 0: [2]_q^2 = h^2 + 4 where h = q - q^{-1}. Proof. (q + q^{-1})^2 = q^2 + 2 + q^{-2} and (q - q^{-1})^2 + 4 = (q^2 - 2 + q^{-2}) + 4 = q^2 + 2 + q^{-2}. Equal. \square

def:classical-limit-functor:
Definition The classical limit functor q \to 1. The classical limit is a monoidal functor \mathcal{L} : \mathbf{C}_q \longrightarrow \mathbf{C}_1 from the braided monoidal category \mathbf{C}_q (at deformation parameter q) to the symmetric monoidal category \mathbf{C}_1 (at q = 1). The functor \mathcal{L} acts on the aether algebra by:

  1. Quantum gap collapse: \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} \to 0, so that the non-commutativity vanishes.
  2. Differential smoothing: The Jackson q-derivative d_q f(z) converges to the ordinary derivative \frac{df}{dz}.
  3. Braiding trivialization: The braiding \sigma_{X,Y} specializes to the symmetric swap \tau_{X,Y}.
rem:classical-limit-functor-remark: Remark Information loss in the classical limit. The classical limit functor \mathcal{L} is exact but not full: quantum information is lost in the limit.
rem:classical-limit-adelic-assembly:

Equivalently, \mathcal{L} is the archimedean component of the realization tower \{\rho_v\}_{v \in \mathrm{Pl}(\mathbb{Q})} of the motivic base ring. Under this reading, \mathbf{C}_q is the universal motive over \widehat{\mathcal{M}}. Each finite place p of \mathbb{Q} (adelic base ring) carries a local realization \rho_p landing in \mathbb{Q}_p. The archimedean place v = \infty carries \rho_\infty = \mathcal{L}, landing in \mathbb{R}. The q \to 1 limit is the vanishing of the local Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon_\infty at the archimedean place. The classical continuum is what remains after that single local \varepsilon_v is collapsed.

Non-fullness of \mathcal{L}: phase decoherence. The full motivic class [X] \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} carries the relative q-phases between all finite places. The archimedean projection \rho_\infty collapses across all those phases, retaining only the real-valued shadow. That collapse is the loss of quantum information: the classical continuum sees only the archimedean projection of the unglued adelic motives.

  1. Planck constant: \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} \to 0.
  2. q-differential: d_q \to d.
  3. Braiding: \mathbf{C}_q degenerates to \mathbf{C}_1, as R(q) \to \mathrm{id} \otimes \mathrm{id}.
  4. Reeb period: \Omega_q \to \infty.

Formally, \mathcal{L} sends A_q to a commutative Hopf algebra A_1 = \mathcal{O}(\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cl}}), the coordinate ring of the classical Bring's curve. The self-duality A_q \simeq \omega_{A_q}^\bullet descends to classical Serre duality.
def:classical-limit-obstruction:
Definition The classical limit obstruction of a quantum universe. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe over a Noetherian ring R with aether parameter q and classical limit functor \mathcal{L} : \mathbf{C}_q \to \mathbf{C}_1 (classical limit functor). The classical limit obstruction of the quantum universe is the Hochschild cohomology group

\mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1)
 := 
HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad})

where \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}) is the Lusztig integral form of the quantized enveloping algebra associated to A, and \mathrm{Ad} denotes the adjoint bimodule.
rem:classical-limit-obstruction-remark: Remark The obstruction as a deformation obstruction. Elements of \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) are obstructions to extending second-order deformations of the Frobenius--Hopf algebra A_q across q = 1.
rem:classical-limit-obstruction-properti:
Remark The Hochschild tower of the classical limit obstruction. The classical limit obstruction sits in a Hochschild tower whose vanishing controls flatness of the q \to 1 deformation.

The Hochschild tower. The Hochschild cohomology groups HH^n(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) govern the deformation theory of the aether family \{A_q\}_{q \in \mathbb{G}_m}:

  • HH^0(\mathrm{Ad}): hidden symmetries.
  • HH^1(\mathrm{Ad}): outer derivations.
  • HH^2(\mathrm{Ad}): obstructions to extending deformations across q = 1.
  • HH^3(\mathrm{Ad}): secondary obstructions.

A property \mathcal{P}(q) persists through q = 1 if and only if its obstruction class [\mathcal{P}] \in HH^2(\mathrm{Ad}) vanishes.

Control of the classical limit by HH^2. The classical limit q \to 1 is a deformation-theoretic specialisation. The obstructions to flatness at each order in (q-1) live in HH^2. Expanding A_q = A_1 + (q-1)\phi_1 + (q-1)^2\phi_2 + \cdots, the first-order deformation \phi_1 is a Hochschild 2-cocycle. The second-order term \phi_2 exists iff [\phi_1] \cup [\phi_1] = 0 in HH^3. The total obstruction to the classical limit is the formal sum \mathrm{obs}_\infty = \sum_{n \geq 1} (q-1)^n [\phi_n] \in HH^2(\mathrm{Ad})[[q-1]]. This formal power series converges iff all Massey products vanish through the tower.

Connection to the brane tower. The Hochschild obstruction [\phi_n] maps to the quantum characteristic class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) under the Hochschild-to-sheaf comparison map. The abstract Hochschild obstruction is computed concretely by the Euler class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) and its Kummer filtration.
rem:classical-limit-topology-free: Remark Topology-free surreal reformulation of the q\to1 limit. Topology-free reformulation (forward reference). The classical limit functor uses a topological q \to 1 limit on the parameter space, which has obstructions (classical limit obstruction). The appendix replaces it with a literal evaluation in Conway's surreal field at q = 1 + \varepsilon, then takes the standard-part. Both replacements are conjectural; if they hold, they remove the need for any analytic machinery on the parameter space.
rem:classical-shadow-of-the-aether:
Remark The classical shadow of the aether: what the obstruction space becomes at q = 1. The classical limit functor \mathcal{L} \colon \mathbf{C}_q \to \mathbf{C}_1 sends the aether at parameter q to its value at q = 1. This remark asks what it does to the classical limit obstruction, the Hochschild cohomology HH^{2}(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}), and the answer is that the shadow is zero.

At the classical point. For q = 1 the aether algebra is the universal enveloping algebra \mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}) of the semisimple Lie algebra \mathfrak{g} (or its dual, the coordinate ring of the group). Its Hochschild cohomology with coefficients in a bimodule M is the Lie algebra cohomology of \mathfrak{g} with coefficients in M made into a \mathfrak{g}-module by the adjoint action, HH^{n}(\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}), M) \cong H^{n}(\mathfrak{g}, M^{\mathrm{ad}}) [cartan1956]. Whitehead's lemmas state that H^{1}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^{2}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0 for \mathfrak{g} semisimple over a field of characteristic zero and M finite-dimensional [weibel1994]; the adjoint bimodule \mathrm{Ad}(A) is a direct sum of finite-dimensional modules, so the vanishing holds for it degree by degree. Hence

  \mathcal{L}\bigl(\mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1)\bigr) \;=\; HH^{2}\bigl(\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}\bigr) \;=\; 0 :

the classical shadow of the obstruction space is the zero space. The only one-dimensional cohomology that \mathrm{SU}(2) does have is H^{3}(\mathfrak{su}_2; k) = k, the Cartan three-form, in degree three and with trivial coefficients; it is an invariant of the group, not a deformation obstruction.

In the formal neighbourhood. Expanding in \hbar = q - 1 rather than evaluating at a fixed q places the aether in the setting of formal deformation theory, where the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem has a q-side companion: Kontsevich's formality theorem identifies the Hochschild cohomology of a formal deformation of a smooth algebra with the Poisson cohomology of its classical limit [kontsevich-2003], and for a symplectic classical limit that Poisson cohomology is de Rham cohomology [nest-tsygan-1995, dolgushev-rubtsov-2005]. In that setting the Hochschild homology and cohomology of the formal aether are computed from the classical shadow, and the shadow of the obstruction is still zero: a formal expansion around q = 1 sees no obstruction line.

At the physical point. At a fixed q \neq 1 neither theorem applies, and the groups have to be computed. What is known is that the untwisted Hochschild theory of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2) has a dimension drop in top degree [feng-tsygan-1991], and that the one-dimensional top group is recovered only in the theory twisted by the Nakayama automorphism [hadfield-krahmer-2005]. No computation in this paper evaluates HH^{2}(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}) at the aether parameter. A one-dimensional obstruction space at q \neq 1 would therefore be a phenomenon of the archimedean evaluation, invisible both at the classical point and in its formal neighbourhood; this is the fibre-versus-observable wall of the introduction, and it is why the one-dimensionality is stated as an axiom of the aether rather than derived from the axioms of a quantum observable universe.
conj:wigner-axiom:
Conjecture The Wigner axiom: a one-dimensional classical-limit obstruction. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with archimedean base curve M_0, and let \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) = HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}) be its classical limit obstruction.

Conjecture (the Wigner axiom). The classical-limit obstruction space is one-dimensional, and its generator is realised by the Euler class of the base:

(W1) \dim_k \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) = 1;

(W2) the archimedean realisation \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) \to H^2(M_0; k) carries a generator w(A) onto the Euler class e(TM_0), which is non-zero; consequently \langle e(TM_0), [M_0] \rangle = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0) is the integer that determines the obstruction.

Why it is an axiom. Two arguments that were offered for (W1) do not go through. The first invoked Poincaré duality for Hochschild cohomology in the untwisted form HH^{2} \cong (HH^{1})^{\vee}; for the Hopf algebras in question the duality that holds is Brown and Zhang's twisted form HH^{i}(H, M) \cong HH_{d-i}(H, {}_{\nu}M) [brown-zhang-2008], cohomology to homology with the Nakayama automorphism \nu on the coefficients, and at q \neq 1 the untwisted version fails outright: the top Hochschild homology of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2) drops, and the one-dimensional top group reappears only after the twist [hadfield-krahmer-2005]. The second counted the deformation direction q as a class in the obstruction space; it is a class in HH^{1}, one degree lower. And at the classical point the statement is false: for \mathfrak{g} semisimple and M finite-dimensional, Whitehead's lemmas give H^{1}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^{2}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0 [weibel1994], so \mathrm{Obs} = 0 at q = 1. One-dimensionality at q \neq 1 is therefore a hypothesis about the aether, not a theorem of the axioms.

Why (W2) has this target. For Bring's surface the symmetry group S_5 acts on everything in sight, and an equivariant realisation must land in the S_5-invariant part of the base's Hochschild theory. That invariant part is k^2 in HH_0 — spanned by H^0(M_0, \mathcal{O}) and H^1(M_0, K) = H^2(M_0; k) — and k in HH^0, and it is zero in HH^2(M_0) = H^1(TM_0), the deformation space of the curve. An equivariant image of a one-dimensional obstruction space among the deformations of the base is therefore zero, and the only invariant line that can carry the integer is H^2(M_0; k), where the Euler class lives. The axiom is stated with that target and no other.

What it buys and what would refute it. Every block that reduces a Millennium-type persistence question to the divisibility n \mid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) is conditional on this axiom. A computation of HH^{2}(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), \mathrm{Ad}) at generic q with dimension different from one refutes (W1); an equivariant realisation whose image of the obstruction line vanishes in H^2(M_0; k) refutes (W2). Neither computation exists in this paper.

The name follows Wigner's Courant lecture of 11 May 1959 on the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics [wigner1960]: the axiom is exactly the assumption that a single scalar of the aether governs the persistence of its structure into the classical world.
thm:qou-obstruction-reduction:
Theorem Conditional on the Wigner-axiom inputs: the obstruction is a single integer \chi_A. Conditional on the Wigner axiom. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with archimedean base curve M_0. Take as hypotheses the following four inputs, which are the content of the Wigner axiom for the classical limit obstruction \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1):

  1. (twisted duality) \dim HH^i(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) = \dim HH_{3-i}(\mathcal{U}_q, {}_\nu\mathrm{Ad}) for 0 \le i \le 3, where \nu is the Nakayama automorphism;
  2. (twisted rigidity) \dim HH_1(\mathcal{U}_q, {}_\nu\mathrm{Ad}) = 1;
  3. (Kummer vanishing) the obstruction vanishes at Kummer level n iff n \mid \kappa_0, for an integer \kappa_0;
  4. (trace) the trace pairing sends the class \chi_A of w(A) to \kappa_0, and the image \varphi_1 of the obstruction class equals that trace.

Then:

(a) \dim HH^2 = 1, and \varphi_1 = \chi_A.

(b) For every n \ge 1, the obstruction vanishes at Kummer level n iff n \mid \chi_A.

The identification \chi_A = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0) is not part of this statement; the proof discusses it.
